text:
alex: Quick heads-up — canary is exercising /v2/generate-json and we're seeing intermittent differences in the structured output. Some responses have "metadata": null, others omit the key entirely. This is breaking a few enterprise SDKs. Anyone seen this?

maria: Which model/variant and content-type are you hitting?

alex: Hitting gptx-compact v2 on canary. Requests are sent with Content-Type: application/json. Example returned payload that failed our SDK: 
```json
{
  "id": "r_123",
  "content": { "text": "ok" },
  "metadata": null
}
```

cheng: I thought our policy was: optional object fields -> omit when empty, only use null for explicit opt-out. Did that change?

sam: SDK 3.x deserializers expect metadata to be an object if present; null currently causes a runtime NPE in some languages (looking at Java/TypeScript interop). There's an open PR (PR-402) adding a null-check, but it's not merged to release yet.

maria: Hmm. If the runtime started returning nulls we need to check the kernel update that touched structured-output postprocessing. @cheng any chance recent sanitizer pass introduced this?

cheng: I tweaked the postproc to reduce allocations — there was a path that normalized empty maps to null to save tokens. That should've been gated. Sorry — pushing a revert in a minute.

alex: Thanks. Short-term: can we add a compatibility shim on the API edge that turns "metadata": null -> {} for canary/hosted until SDKs roll? Safer than forcing all clients to update immediately.

maria: Yes — we can add a cheap post-transform at the JSON marshal layer: if (field == null && fieldSchema.type == "object") -> output {}. I'll open a small change and attach to the canary rollout.

sam: I'll also update SDK PR to tolerate null (coerce to empty object) and cut a patch release after canary stabilizes.

qa-bot: Added regression test "response-metadata-null-handling" to CI pipeline. Current run failed on the null-case — flagged to @maria.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: redwood-canary-1 -> v2026.03.17 (contains postproc revert + shim)

maria: Merged shim change to canary branch. Please monitor schema-violations dashboard (Console -> Contracts). I'll add a note in the changelog and a short blurb in the API compatibility doc.

alex: One more question — should we be enforcing Content-Type header more strictly? Some clients send "application/json; charset=utf-8" and others "application/json"; we currently accept both but downstream parsing differs.

cheng: I'd prefer permissive matching (startsWith "application/json") but normalize before parsing. We should add a unit test in runtime to ensure both are accepted and produce identical outputs.

sam: SDK will also normalize headers. I'll include a test matrix for both header variants.

maria: Cool. Follow-ups: 1) monitor canary for 2 hours, 2) merge SDK patch once canary green, 3) add a lint to contract-checker asserting optional objects are omitted not null (but allow explicit null when documented). I'll create the issues.

alex: Awesome — thanks everyone. Ping me if any customers flag breakages so we can expedite. :thumbsup:
